# Ledger Requirements and Design

**CP1 — 19 October 2026**

**Team members:** Yichang Chen, Yiran Tao, Haonan Bai, Yijia Wang

## 1. Project Description

Ledger is a native Android application for students, roommates, and friends who need personal expense records and shared-expense coordination. Personal Account Management supports manual entry, statement import, receipt recognition, duplicate review, and historical currency conversion. Expense Group Management supports invitations and shared expenses. The planned Let's Go Dutch feature will let members claim receipt item units collaboratively and receive live allocation updates.

The current app opens **My Expenses** and has three navigation tabs: **My Expenses**, **Group**, and **Me**. My Expenses uses an installation-local personal ledger and is available without signing in. Group and Me require a Ledger session. Signing in normally returns to My Expenses; an outstanding invitation continues to its preview and acceptance flow. Signing out returns to My Expenses.

Personal transactions are stored in Android SQLite. They are not associated with the signed-in account, migrated on sign-in, synchronized to MongoDB, or linked to group expenses. Signing out or changing accounts does not switch or clear this local ledger. Group membership and shared expenses are stored in MongoDB and accessed through authenticated backend APIs. Recognition returns suggestions for review; Android validates and saves personal transactions, while the backend validates and calculates shared-expense allocations.

**Scope convention:** “Implemented” means present in the current repository, not proof that a particular deployed server or APK has been updated. “Planned” describes a target requirement and proposed design. Planned endpoints, storage, and live events below are not current API contracts.

## 2. Requirements Specification

### 2.1. Features and Current Scope

| Feature | Implemented scope | Planned extension |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Authentication and Account Management** — supporting functionality | Email/password and Google registration and sign-in; account information; revocable sessions; sign-out. | Authentication and quota integration for shared deployment of paid document recognition. |
| **Feature 1 — Personal Account Management** | Local income/expense entry, editing and deletion; CSV import on Android; supported text-PDF statement parsing on the backend; optional OpenAI receipt/statement recognition; editable import review; duplicate suggestions; historical FX quotes and local conversion. | Account-bound storage, cloud synchronization, and reuse of a personal record in a group are not implemented. |
| **Feature 2 — Expense Group Management** | Create and list groups; generate, preview, and accept invitations; rename groups; owner-authorized group deletion; manually create and edit shared expenses; Equal split and Custom amounts; spending totals and allocated shares. | Personal-bill reuse, percentage and itemized splits, repayments and net balances, and settlement-based archival. |
| **Feature 3 — Let's Go Dutch** | No group live-claiming workflow is implemented. | Start a split session; claim/unclaim item units; live allocation updates; reconnect recovery; finalize allocations. |

Personal Account Management supports CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, CNY, and JPY. Expense groups currently support CAD, USD, EUR, and CNY and retain the currency selected at creation. A shared expense is entered directly in that group currency; there is no group FX or personal-record selection step.

**Figure 1 — Retained use case overview.** The image does not distinguish implemented and planned workflows. Its Group Owner associations do not express all current permissions: any Group Member can invite, rename, and create an expense, while only the owner can delete the group. ### 2.3. Actors

| Actor | Responsibility and access |
| --- | --- |
| **User** | A person using Ledger, with or without an account. Can use the installation-local Personal Account Management feature and choose to register or sign in. |
| **Authenticated User** | A User with a valid Ledger session. Can view account information, create/list their groups, and preview or accept an invitation. |
| **Group Member** | An Authenticated User included in an active group's membership. Can view its expenses, create a shared expense, generate invitations, and rename the group. Can edit a shared expense they created. Planned live claims and repayments belong to this role. |
| **Group Owner** | The group creator, who is also a Group Member. Can delete the group and edit any expense in it. Starting/finalizing live split sessions and settlement-based archival are planned owner actions. |
| **Google Authentication** | Provides Google identity evidence verified by User Management. Ledger issues its own session after verification. |
| **OpenAI Document Recognition** | Extracts transaction suggestions from explicitly submitted images/PDFs. Current receipt extraction returns a transaction for the receipt total, not claimable item units. |
| **Exchange-rate Service (Frankfurter / ECB)** | Supplies historical exchange-rate quotes. Expense Management uses those quotes to calculate reporting-currency amounts on Android. |

Role permissions are contextual: ownership of one group does not grant access to another. Opening an invitation alone does not join a group; the user must sign in and explicitly accept it.

### 2.4. Use Case Descriptions

#### Authentication and Account Management — Supporting Functionality

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Sign In** | Sign in with a Ledger email/password or Google. A successful sign-in enables Group and Me and normally returns to My Expenses; a pending invitation continues instead. The local personal ledger remains the same. |
| **Register an Account** | Create an account with an email, password, and display name, or confirm a verified Google profile. Duplicate/conflicting accounts are rejected; an email account is not automatically linked to Google. |
| **View Account Information** | View the authenticated account's display name, email, sign-in methods, account creation date, and session expiry under Me. |
| **Sign Out** | Clear the local session and return to My Expenses. Attempt server-session revocation; if the network is unavailable, the server session still expires at its configured expiry. |

#### Feature 1 — Personal Account Management

| Use case | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Import and Review a Receipt (UC-01)** | Explicitly submit a receipt image for OpenAI Document Recognition through the backend, then review/correct transaction fields and warnings on Android. Recognition creates no saved financial record. |
| **Import a Bank Statement** | Parse supported CSV formats on Android, or submit a supported text PDF to the backend's statement parser. OpenAI extraction is an explicit alternative for documents. Review up to 200 candidate transactions before saving selected entries locally. “Local statement” parsing means parsing within the Ledger backend without external AI; it still requires a network request. |
| **Manually Add an Entry** | Enter an income or expense with amount, currency, date, merchant, category, and optional notes. Review validation and duplicate suggestions before saving to SQLite. |
| **Review and Edit Personal Records** | Browse, filter, edit, and delete local records. Revision checks protect edits and deletion from stale local data. There is no existing group-expense link to update. |
| **Resolve Duplicate Candidates (UC-02)** | Compare draft entries with local records and other selected import rows. Review amount/date/merchant evidence, skip a candidate row or explicitly keep it, then commit selected valid entries locally. |
| **Convert Currency** | Convert original amounts to a chosen reporting currency using historical quotes, preserving the original amount, rate, effective date, and source. Cached quotes can be reused offline. |

#### Feature 2 — Expense Group Management

| Use case | Status and description |
| --- | --- |
| **Create an Expense Group** | Implemented. An Authenticated User supplies a name and currency, optionally a description. The creator becomes the owner and first member. |
| **Invite and Join Group Members** | Implemented. Any Group Member can generate an invitation. An authenticated invitee previews and explicitly accepts a valid invitation. Repeated acceptance does not duplicate membership; groups allow up to 100 members. |
| **Rename an Expense Group** | Implemented. Any Group Member can update the group name. |
| **Record and View a Shared Expense** | Implemented. Any Group Member manually enters a description, group-currency amount, payer, participants, and split mode. The backend calculates/stores shares. The app retrieves spending totals and allocated shares. |
| **Edit a Shared Expense** | Implemented. The expense creator or Group Owner can edit it. A changed update must match the saved revision; an identical submission returns the existing record without another write. |
| **Delete an Expense Group** | Implemented. Only the Group Owner can soft-delete it. It disappears from members' active lists and its invitations stop working. This action has no settlement prerequisite and provides no read-only archive interface. |
| **Reuse and Split a Personal Bill (UC-03)** | Planned. Select a personal transaction, explicitly confirm the information to share, and create an independent group-expense snapshot. Cross-currency reuse requires a reviewed quote. No source-record API or linkage exists yet. |
| **Choose an Extended Split Method** | Planned. Add percentage and itemized rules beyond the currently implemented Equal split and Custom amounts. Itemized allocation will use Let's Go Dutch. |
| **Record and Confirm a Repayment** | Planned. Record a payment between members and obtain the recipient's confirmation before updating net balances. Ledger will record payments, not transfer money. |
| **Archive an Expense Group** | Planned. Make a settled group read-only while preserving expense and repayment history. Archival is a separate lifecycle requirement from the implemented deletion action. |

The current **Allocated shares** summary is the sum of each member's expense allocations. It does not calculate who owes whom, subtract amounts paid, or account for repayments. Other members see changes when opening the group or using **Refresh**; there is no group push notification or automatic live synchronization.

#### Feature 3 — Let's Go Dutch — Planned

| Use case | Planned description |
| --- | --- |
| **Start a Split Session** | A Group Owner starts a live session from a reviewed, reconciled itemized receipt. A new item-unit representation is required; the current receipt extractor supplies transaction totals only. |
| **Claim or Unclaim Receipt Items Live (UC-04)** | A Group Member claims an available unit or releases their own unit. At most one member can own a unit. |
| **View Live Allocations and Totals** | Members receive accepted changes automatically. Pending actions, unassigned amounts, and finalized allocations are distinguished. |
| **Recover Live State After Reconnect (UC-05)** | Retrieve authoritative state and resolve pending operations after a disconnect or missed event without applying a financial operation twice. |
| **Finalize a Split Session** | A Group Owner finalizes only when required units are assigned and shares equal the total. Finalization posts the allocation once and closes the session to claims. |

### 2.5. Formal Use Case Specifications

#### UC-01 — Import and Review a Receipt

**Status:** Implemented, subject to backend OpenAI configuration and availability.

**Primary actor:** User.

**Preconditions:** The user has a readable receipt image and can reach the configured backend. Sign-in is not required by the current guest ledger service.

**Postcondition:** Editable candidate transactions and warnings are shown on Android. No personal transaction has been saved; UC-02 covers confirmation and commit.

**Main success scenario**

1. The user opens **Import** from My Expenses and selects a supported receipt image.
2. The app explains the external processing and the user chooses **Send to OpenAI & extract**.
3. Expense Management validates the selection and sends `fileName`, `mimeType`, `dataBase64`, and `defaultCurrency` to `POST /api/ledger/imports/preview`.
4. Bill Import validates the file and resource limits, then calls OpenAI Document Recognition through `OpenAiDocumentExtractor`.
5. The service returns transaction candidates and warnings. A receipt is represented by its total, including tax/tip, rather than separate item units.
6. Expense Management validates the candidate structure and displays editable amount, currency, date, merchant, kind, category, and notes. The user corrects missing or inaccurate values.
7. Expense Management checks the edited rows and computes duplicate suggestions against the local ledger and selected import rows.
8. The app stays in import review for selection, duplicate acknowledgement, and the explicit save action in UC-02.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — Cancellation:** No extraction request is sent before confirmation; canceling review saves no transaction.
- **3a/4a — Invalid file:** Empty/invalid data or an invalid name is rejected; unsupported content/type yields 415, and excessive size may yield 400 or 413 depending on the failed validation. The maximum document size is 5 MiB.
- **4b — Service unavailable:** Missing configuration, timeout, or upstream failure shows an error and permits retry/manual entry. Rate limits return 429; exhausted extraction capacity returns 503.
- **5a — Invalid or empty extraction:** Show the returned warning/error and request a clearer document or manual entry. Missing financial values are not invented.
- **6a/7a — Invalid fields or duplicate suggestions:** Keep the rows in review. Invalid selected rows and unacknowledged duplicate candidates cannot be committed.

There is no backend import-draft record, draft revision, duplicate-search endpoint, or personal-ledger write in this use case.

#### UC-02 — Resolve Duplicate Candidates

**Status:** Implemented.

**Primary actor:** User.

**Preconditions:** A receipt/statement/CSV import preview exists in the Android app. Existing records are scoped to the current installation.

**Postcondition:** Selected valid rows and their request result are committed atomically to SQLite, or no selected row is inserted.

**Main success scenario**

1. Expense Management loads existing local records and reviews the current import rows using `LedgerDomain.review`.
2. The app shows duplicate candidates with matching amount, date, and merchant evidence. Scores are heuristic indicators, not probabilities.
3. The user skips rows they do not want and explicitly acknowledges any duplicate candidates they choose to keep. Selected invalid rows are corrected.
4. The app calls `LedgerRepository.commitImport(rows, source, fileName, requestId)` with the current selections and acknowledgements.
5. Expense Management checks the persisted request fingerprint. A matching completed request returns its saved count; a new request is revalidated against the current local records and selected batch.
6. Expense Management obtains any required historical quote from its cache or Bill Import, computes converted minor units locally, and validates totals before inserting records.
7. One SQLite transaction inserts all accepted records and the request result. The backend stores neither the records nor the import result.
8. The app reports the number imported and returns to the local transaction list.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — No matches:** No duplicate acknowledgement is required; normal field validation and explicit confirmation still apply.
- **3a — A separate purchase resembles an existing one:** The user can keep both; suggestions never force a merge.
- **5a — Reused request ID with changed content:** Reject it locally. This is a `LedgerException`, not an HTTP 409 from a personal-transaction API.
- **5b — Current records reveal an unacknowledged duplicate or invalid row:** Stop before inserting; retain the review for correction.
- **6a — Required FX unavailable:** Save no selected records; keep the draft available for retry.
- **7a — SQLite failure:** Roll back the entire record/request transaction. A retry of an already committed identical request returns its original result without reinserting records.

Manual entry uses the same local validation and duplicate suggestions, but saves through `LedgerRepository.save` rather than the import-batch interface.

#### UC-03 — Reuse and Split a Personal Bill

**Status:** Planned; not implemented for CP1. Manual shared-expense creation is the current baseline.

**Primary actor:** Group Member, including Group Owner.

**Preconditions:** The user has a valid session, belongs to an active group, and selects a reviewed personal transaction from this Android installation. Payer and participants are current members.

**Postcondition:** An explicitly approved group-expense snapshot and canonical allocations are saved once. Later edits to the local personal record do not silently change the group expense.

**Main success scenario - proposed**

1. The member chooses a future Add from my records action. Android Expense Management reads the personal record and its revision from local SQLite; the backend does not query personal records by account or source ID.
2. The member reviews the selected amount, date, merchant, and other details, chooses the payer, participants, and Equal split or Custom amounts, and explicitly approves sharing those fields.
3. The app sends the approved snapshot and split inputs to a proposed reuse-preview interface. Group Bill Splitting authenticates the caller and validates active membership, payer, participants, and submitted values. A local record ID is not a backend lookup key.
4. If currencies differ, the proposed group-conversion workflow obtains a historical quote through Bill Import. Group Bill Splitting calculates a group-currency preview; the app shows the rate, effective date, converted total, and canonical shares for review. This integration is planned.
5. Before final confirmation, Android rechecks the local source revision. The member confirms the preview; the app submits the approved snapshot and allocations with the same retry-safe request ID. The backend revalidates membership, values, any quote, and shares.
6. Group Bill Splitting persists the independent group-expense snapshot, canonical allocations, and request result. An identical retry returns the existing result; conflicting reuse of the request ID is rejected.
7. The app retrieves the updated group summary through REST. Other members currently see changes when opening or explicitly refreshing the group; live delivery is a separate planned capability in UC-04/UC-05.

**Failure scenarios - proposed**

- **1a/2a — Missing source or canceled sharing:** Submit no snapshot and save no group expense.
- **3a/4a — Invalid membership, split, or unavailable quote:** Reject the preview and keep the expense uncommitted.
- **5a — Source, group, or preview changed:** Require renewed confirmation. Android checks the local source revision; the backend validates only the submitted snapshot and group state.
- **6a — Lost response:** Retry the same request ID and confirmed content. Conflicting reuse of a request ID is rejected.
- **6b — Persistence failure:** Do not report success before the expense is committed.

**Current baseline:** CP1 supports manual shared-expense creation with Equal split or Custom amounts and REST summary retrieval. Personal-record selection, the reuse-preview contract, group FX conversion, and live group events remain planned.

#### UC-04 — Claim or Unclaim Receipt Items Live

**Status:** Planned; the following behavior and interfaces are proposed.

**Primary actor:** Group Member.

**Preconditions:** The member belongs to an active group with an open, reconciled itemized split session. The app has an authoritative version and an authenticated live subscription.

**Postcondition:** An accepted claim/release changes one unit's owner and its derived allocations exactly once; subscribers receive the committed state.

**Main success scenario**

1. The member opens the session and sees available units, owners, and totals.
2. The member selects Claim on an available unit or Unclaim on their own unit.
3. The app marks the action pending and sends `unitId`, `action`, `version`, and `operationKey` to the proposed claim endpoint.
4. Group Bill Splitting uses User Management to authenticate the caller, then verifies membership, session status, and expected version.
5. A conditional update assigns/releases the unit. Only one conflicting claimant can succeed.
6. One transaction persists the updated allocations, sequence, event, and operation result.
7. After commit, the backend acknowledges the caller and publishes **`onGroupUpdated`** to authorized subscribers.
8. Apps apply each event once in sequence order and replace pending previews with canonical allocations.

**Failure scenarios**

- **4a — Finalized session or lost membership:** Reject the change and refresh/leave the session.
- **5a — Taken unit or stale version:** Return 409 with current state and undo the pending preview.
- **5b — Releasing another member's unit:** Return 403 and make no change.
- **6a — Lost acknowledgement:** Resolve/retry the same operation key and payload; do not generate a second operation automatically.
- **8a — Duplicate/out-of-order event:** Ignore duplicates; recover a gap through UC-05 instead of guessing state.

#### UC-05 — Recover Live State After Reconnect

**Status:** Planned; this is not the current manual Refresh workflow.

**Primary actor:** Group Member.

**Preconditions:** The app knows the group ID, last applied sequence, and pending operation keys. The user can establish a valid session.

**Postcondition:** The app installs a consistent snapshot, reconciles pending operations, and resumes ordered live updates.

**Main success scenario**

1. The app detects disconnection or a sequence gap, labels the group view as reconnecting, and pauses new live writes.
2. It reconnects with the Ledger session. The backend rechecks identity and current group membership before subscribing it.
3. The app buffers arriving `onGroupUpdated` events and requests a consistent snapshot with a sequence watermark.
4. Group Bill Splitting returns the authorized snapshot of expenses, claims, allocation/settlement state, and sequence.
5. The app installs the snapshot, discards buffered events at or below the watermark, and applies only contiguous later events.
6. The app resolves pending operation keys. A missing operation may be retried with its original payload and version.
7. When recovery completes, the app labels the view live and enables new claims.

**Failure scenarios**

- **2a — Expired session:** Require reauthentication before restoring protected live state.
- **2b — Lost membership:** Stop the subscription and discard inaccessible group state.
- **3a — Another connection failure:** Keep a clearly labelled stale view, disable new live writes, and retry with bounded backoff.
- **5a — Remaining gap or unavailable replay:** Request a fresh snapshot; do not extrapolate allocations or balances.
- **6a — Unresolved operation:** Keep the action labelled pending until lookup/idempotent retry establishes its result.

### 2.6. Non-Functional Requirements

| Requirement | Target and rationale | Current boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **NFR-1 — Financial Integrity** | Accepted shares must sum exactly to the expense total, and retries must not duplicate a saved financial operation. Planned item claims must have at most one owner per unit. Zero discrepancy is required for trustworthy accounting. | Integer monetary arithmetic, deterministic equal splits, custom-sum validation, request deduplication, and edit revisions are implemented. Live claims and settlement invariants remain planned. |
| **NFR-2 — Access Control and Privacy** | Every protected request/subscription must verify identity and ownership/membership. Release traffic must use HTTPS; future live traffic must use WSS. Recognition requires explicit submission. | Account/group routes use session and role checks. Personal records are installation-local. Current `/api/ledger/*` services are guest endpoints with resource limits, not session-protected services. Authenticated paid-service access and live-subscription checks remain work for shared deployment/live features. “Every protected path” is a design obligation, not a claim of measured 100% test coverage. |
| **NFR-3 — Real-Time Responsiveness** | For up to 20 members and 200 item units, 95% of accepted live changes should appear within 2 seconds, and recovery should restore consistent state within 5 seconds. These proposed limits cover a large shared meal. | A future acceptance target, not a measured result. Current groups refresh through REST; background requests, timeouts, and bounded work support responsiveness. |

## 3. Design Specification

### 3.1. Domain Components and Responsibility Boundaries

The backend is one Express/TypeScript application with **four logical domain components**: **User Management**, **Group and Invitation Management**, **Group Bill Splitting**, and **Bill Import**. Shared routing, validation, persistence adapters, and middleware support these responsibility boundaries. The source files below implement them within one deployment; the names do not imply separate service classes.

The original component names are retained wherever applicable. **Expense Management** names the personal accounting domain, which currently runs on Android. The old diagram's placement of that component in the backend remains a documented mismatch.

| Retained figure label | Meaning used consistently in this text | Correspondence limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User Management | Backend account authentication, profiles, and Ledger sessions. | Current responsibilities also include email/password accounts, beyond the Google sign-in path shown. |
| Bill Import | Backend document extraction/parsing and historical FX quote services. | Its current `/api/ledger/*` scope includes quotes; personal review, duplicate checking, and commit belong to Android. |
| Expense Management | Android personal accounting domain and SQLite state. | Its old backend placement and group-expense persistence responsibility do not match the implementation. |
| Group Bill Splitting | Backend shared-expense creation/editing, split calculations, and summaries. | Personal-record reuse and live synchronization in the old figures remain planned. |
| Android front-end / front-end | Android client, including UI/controllers and Expense Management. | The old images do not show the client's local accounting and storage boundary. |
| Google Authentication | Google identity verification used by User Management. | Ledger issues its own session after identity verification. |
| OCR Service / AI Service / AI Bill Recognition | Document-recognition roles currently supplied by **OpenAI Document Recognition**. | These legacy labels do not denote separate current OCR and AI integrations. |
| Exchange-rate Service / Exchange-rate (External API) | **Exchange-rate Service**, currently provided by Frankfurter / ECB. | Bill Import retrieves quotes; Expense Management converts personal amounts on Android. |
| Database | MongoDB for backend account/group state; SQLite for Android personal state. | The old single backend database symbol cannot represent both deployment locations. |

**Group and Invitation Management** is required by the current app but has no separate box in the retained dependency diagram. It is explicitly defined below.

#### User Management

- **Responsibility:** Register and authenticate email/password and Google accounts; prevent conflicting identities; return account profiles; issue, validate, and revoke Ledger sessions.
- **Owned data:** MongoDB `users` and `sessions`. Passwords use salted scrypt hashes; only SHA-256 session-token hashes are persisted. Sessions expire after seven days.
- **Interfaces:** `/api/auth/*`, `GET /api/users/me`, `requireSession(users, sessions)`, `startSession(sessions, user)`, and user-store lookups.
- **Dependencies:** Google Authentication and MongoDB. Group components use its session middleware and profile lookups. It does not own the local personal ledger or calculate shared-expense allocations.
- **Source:** [accountAuth.ts](../backend/src/accountAuth.ts), [googleAuth.ts](../backend/src/googleAuth.ts), [session.ts](../backend/src/session.ts), [userStore.ts](../backend/src/userStore.ts), [password.ts](../backend/src/password.ts).

#### Group and Invitation Management

- **Responsibility:** Create/list active groups; manage names, membership, invitation generation/preview/acceptance, and owner-authorized soft deletion. Maintain invitation expiry and the 100-member limit.
- **Owned data:** MongoDB `groups` and `groupinvitations`. Invitations use random tokens with seven-day expiry; only token hashes are persisted. Group creation is deduplicated by owner and creation request ID.
- **Interfaces:** Group creation/listing, invitation routes, rename/delete routes, and the public invitation/App Link landing routes described below.
- **Dependencies:** User Management for authenticated identity and inviter/member names; MongoDB for group and invitation state. Group Bill Splitting reads its active membership, owner, and currency data. Invitation acceptance is separate from preview.
- **Source:** [groupManagement.ts](../backend/src/groupManagement.ts), group/invitation schemas in [groupStore.ts](../backend/src/groupStore.ts), and the group-list route currently housed in [groupExpenses.ts](../backend/src/groupExpenses.ts). File placement does not change domain ownership.

#### Group Bill Splitting

- **Responsibility:** Validate and create/edit shared expenses; enforce creator/owner edit permissions; compute Equal split and Custom amounts; deduplicate submissions; enforce changed-edit revisions; aggregate spending and allocated shares.
- **Owned data:** MongoDB `expenses`, including canonical shares and request IDs in each expense document. The component reads groups and public member names but does not create memberships or own user accounts.
- **Interfaces:** Expense POST/PUT and group-summary GET routes; `parseMoney` and `splitBill` for authoritative monetary calculations.
- **Dependencies:** User Management, group data owned by Group and Invitation Management, and MongoDB. It currently has no dependency on Expense Management or Bill Import because group expenses are entered in the group currency.
- **Planned extension:** Item-unit sessions, claims, percentage/itemized allocations, operation-result/event storage, authenticated live delivery/recovery, and repayments/net balances. The proposed UC-04/UC-05 behavior belongs here; it is not implemented by the retained M1 Socket.IO relay.
- **Source:** [groupExpenses.ts](../backend/src/groupExpenses.ts), [splitting.ts](../backend/src/splitting.ts), and the expense schema/serializer in [groupStore.ts](../backend/src/groupStore.ts).

#### Bill Import

The figure-compatible name is retained for the current `backend/src/ledger` document and quote services. This component also provides historical FX quotes used by Android personal accounting.

- **Responsibility:** Expose import capabilities; validate uploaded document metadata/signatures/size; obtain transaction suggestions from OpenAI Document Recognition; parse supported text-PDF statements within the backend; retrieve and validate historical Exchange-rate Service (Frankfurter / ECB) quotes.
- **Owned data:** No persistent personal financial records. The service keeps bounded in-memory quote caches and request/concurrency counters. Uploaded documents and recognition results are returned for review and are not persisted by Ledger's backend.
- **Interfaces:** `/api/ledger/meta`, `/api/ledger/exchange`, `/api/ledger/imports/preview`, and `/api/ledger/imports/statement-preview`.
- **Dependencies:** OpenAI Document Recognition, Exchange-rate Service (Frankfurter / ECB), and `pdfjs-dist`. It does not call MongoDB to save import drafts, duplicate decisions, personal records, or group expenses. Current routes do not invoke `requireSession`.
- **Source:** [router.ts](../backend/src/ledger/router.ts), [providers.ts](../backend/src/ledger/providers.ts), [statements.ts](../backend/src/ledger/statements.ts), and [importPolicy.ts](../backend/src/ledger/importPolicy.ts).

#### Android Responsibilities

**Android front-end** names the client as a whole in this text and the sequence diagrams. Within it, **Account and Group UI** coordinates authentication, invitations, groups, and manual expense forms through account/group API clients. **Expense Management** owns the local accounting domain: CSV parsing, editable drafts, duplicate scoring, monetary conversion, validation, local revisions, request replay, and SQLite transactions. The screen is named **My Expenses**; Expense Management is the component name, and Personal Account Management is the feature name.

Expense Management is implemented by `LedgerViewModel`, its controllers, `LedgerRepository`, `LedgerDomain` and supporting domain classes, `LedgerDatabase`, and `LedgerHttpRemote`. UI/controller classes coordinate actions; the repository/domain/database own local accounting operations. A local draft is not a backend entity. Bill Import returns suggestions/quotes; the Android component decides what becomes a personal transaction after user confirmation.

### 3.2. Databases and State Ownership

#### MongoDB — Backend Account and Group State

| Collection | Main fields and constraints | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users` | Unique normalized email; display name; optional password hash; optional unique Google ID; timestamps. | User Management |
| `sessions` | Unique token hash; user ID; expiry with TTL index and request-time expiry checks. | User Management |
| `groups` | Name, description, owner ID, member IDs, currency, creation request ID, `deletedAt`, timestamps. Unique owner/creation-request index. | Group and Invitation Management |
| `groupinvitations` | Unique token hash; group ID; inviter ID; expiry with TTL index and request-time validation. Mongoose model: `GroupInvitation`. | Group and Invitation Management |
| `expenses` | Group ID; integer `amountCents`; currency; description; payer; creator/latest editor; `splitMode`; embedded `shares`; `requestId`; `__v` revision; timestamps. Unique group/creator/request index. | Group Bill Splitting |

An expense and its shares are written as one document; the current implementation does not atomically write a separate event log, operation collection, or group sequence. Summary aggregation uses one `$facet` over the group's expenses: totals and allocations include all expenses, while the returned expense list is limited to the latest 50.

#### SQLite — Android Expense Management

The installation-local database is `ledger_guest.db`.

| Table | Purpose and constraints |
| --- | --- |
| `ledger_records` | Personal record ID, revision, serialized input/conversion/source metadata, date, and creation time. Conditional edits/deletes use the expected revision. |
| `ledger_requests` | Unique request ID, canonical input fingerprint, and committed result for local save/import replay. Records and request result commit in one SQLite transaction. |
| `ledger_preferences` | Reporting-currency preference, defaulting to CAD. A reporting-currency change updates records and preference atomically after obtaining required quotes. |
| `ledger_rates` | Quotes indexed by currency pair and requested date, with effective date, source, and fetch time. Supports offline reuse and refresh of provisional current-day quotes. |

Personal money uses integer minor units: JPY has no fractional minor units and the other supported personal currencies have two decimal places. Conversion uses decimal arithmetic and defined rounding on Android. The app's database is excluded from Android backup/device transfer; clearing app data or uninstalling removes it. Raw receipt/statement files are not stored in the database.

**Planned state:** Claimable units, split sessions, repayment records, net balances, event sequences, and operation lookup/replay require new backend schemas and consistency rules. No such collections are part of the current data model.

### 3.3. External Modules

| Module | Current interface and purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Google Authentication** | `verifyGoogleToken(idToken, audience)` uses `google-auth-library` to verify Google tokens and obtain verified identity evidence. | Used by User Management; Ledger issues its own session rather than using the Google token as a group API session. |
| **OpenAI Document Recognition** | `OpenAiDocumentExtractor.extract(file, defaultCurrency): Promise<Extraction>` calls the Responses API with structured transaction output. | Used by Bill Import after explicit submission. Requires backend-only configuration. Current receipt output is a transaction total, not an itemized claiming model. |
| **Exchange-rate Service (Frankfurter / ECB)** | `FrankfurterFxProvider.quote(from, to, date): Promise<ExchangeQuote>` requests historical rates from Frankfurter. | Implemented. Returns `{rate, date, source}`; Expense Management performs amount conversion. A prior effective date is accepted only within the configured seven-day tolerance. |
| **PDF.js (`pdfjs-dist`)** | `extractStatement(file)` parses supported text-PDF statement layouts and checks reconciliation within Ledger's backend process. | Implemented for supported Chase/Amex layouts. No external AI request; this is not offline Android PDF parsing or universal PDF/OCR support. |

### 3.4. Main Interfaces

#### Conventions

All `/api/groups/*` routes, including invitation preview/acceptance, require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Profile retrieval and logout also require a session. Current ledger services are guest routes. API errors generally return `{error}`; local Expense Management errors are exceptions shown by the app, not HTTP responses.

`Session` denotes `{token, expiresAt, user}`. `ExchangeQuote` denotes `{rate, date, source}` with the rate as decimal text. `Extraction` denotes `{candidates: [{rowId, input, warnings}], warnings}`, where `input` has `kind`, `amount`, `currency`, `date`, `merchant`, `category`, and `notes`. No current receipt-item array is included.

#### User Management — Implemented HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Successful result and purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/auth/register` | `email, password, displayName` | 201 `Session`; create a password account. |
| `POST /api/auth/login` | `email, password` | 200 `Session`; sign in to an existing password account. |
| `POST /api/auth/google` | `idToken` | 200 `{status: "signed-in", ...Session}` or `{status: "registration-required", profile}`. |
| `POST /api/auth/google/register` | `idToken, displayName?` | 201 signed-in session for a new account; 200 for an existing Google identity. |
| `GET /api/users/me` | Bearer session | 200 `{user}`; authenticated account profile. |
| `POST /api/auth/logout` | Bearer session | 204; revoke the current session. |

Invalid credentials/session return 401; invalid registration fields return 400; an existing/conflicting identity can return 409. Google identity verification also checks that the email is verified.

#### Group and Invitation Management — Implemented HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Successful result and permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups` | `name, description?, currency?, requestId` | 201 `{group, invitation}`; any Authenticated User creates a group. Default currency CAD. Matching retry returns 200 and may generate a new invitation. |
| `GET /api/groups` | Bearer session | 200 `{groups}`; active groups containing the caller. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/invitations` | Group ID and session | 201 `{invitation}`; any Group Member generates links/token and expiry. |
| `GET /api/groups/invitations/{token}` | Invitation token and session | 200 `{group, inviterName, expiresAt, alreadyMember}`; preview without joining. |
| `POST /api/groups/invitations/{token}/accept` | Invitation token and session | 200 `{group}`; add the caller once, subject to the member limit. |
| `PUT /api/groups/{groupId}/name` | `name` and session | 200 `{group}`; any Group Member renames the group. |
| `DELETE /api/groups/{groupId}` | Group ID and session | 204; Group Owner only, soft deletion. |
| `GET /invite/{token}` | Invitation token; public web route | HTML invitation fallback containing group/inviter information and a link into the app. It grants no group membership or expense access. |
| `GET /.well-known/assetlinks.json` | Public web request | Android App Link association document; no account or expense data. |

#### Group Bill Splitting — Implemented HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Successful result and permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses` | `description, amount, paidBy, splitMode, shares[], requestId` | 201 `{expense}`, or 200 for an identical retry. Any Group Member can create an expense. |
| `PUT /api/groups/{groupId}/expenses/{expenseId}` | `description, amount, paidBy, splitMode, shares[], revision` | 200 `{expense}`; expense creator or Group Owner only. Changed stale update returns 409. |
| `GET /api/groups/{groupId}/summary` | Group ID and session | 200 `{group, totalCents, expenseCount, memberShares, expenses, recentLimit}`; Group Members only. `group` includes public member names/roles; recent expense cards include `canEdit`. |

`amount` and custom share amounts cross the API as decimal text. `splitMode` is `equal` or `custom`; `shares` identifies participants as `{userId, amount?}`. Stored/returned allocations are `{userId, amountCents}`. Payer and participants must belong to the group; participants must be unique and number between 1 and 100. Group currency is obtained from the group, not supplied independently on the expense. `memberShares` represents allocated spending, not net debt.

#### Bill Import — Implemented HTTP Interfaces

| Interface | Input | Successful result and purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/ledger/meta` | None | 200 `{currencies, categories, documentImportAvailable, localStatementImportAvailable, maxDocumentBytes}`; expose capabilities. |
| `GET /api/ledger/exchange` | Query `from, to, date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200 `ExchangeQuote`; historical date from 1999-01-04 through today (UTC). Returns a rate, not a converted amount. |
| `POST /api/ledger/imports/preview` | `fileName, mimeType, dataBase64, defaultCurrency` | 200 `Extraction`; OpenAI receipt/statement recognition, with no database write. |
| `POST /api/ledger/imports/statement-preview` | Same document payload | 200 `Extraction`; supported text-PDF parsing within the backend, without external AI. |

Documents are limited to 5 MiB and validated against JPEG, PNG, WebP, or PDF signatures; the statement parser additionally requires a supported text PDF. Extraction returns at most 200 candidates. Both document endpoints share a maximum of two active extractions, with separate request-rate limits. CSV parsing remains on Android and uses no import HTTP endpoint.

There are no implemented `/api/imports/{draftId}/*`, `/api/transactions`, or `/api/fx/convert` routes. Personal draft review, duplicate scoring, commit, and conversion are Android operations described next.

#### Internal Component Interfaces — Current Source Entry Points

These are existing code boundaries, not additional public APIs. MongoDB model operations shown below are called within the backend routes; the four logical components have not been refactored into separate service classes.

| Component | Interface or entry point | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User Management | `requireSession(users, sessions): RequestHandler` | Verify token hash, expiry, and user; populate authenticated request locals. |
| User Management | `startSession(sessions, user)`; `users.findById(userId)` | Create session data; retrieve identity/profile data for authorized callers. |
| Group and Invitation Management | `groupManagementRouter(users)`; `groupJson(group)` | Expose group/invitation lifecycle routes and group serialization; rely on the parent group's session middleware. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `groupExpensesRouter(users, sessions)` | Mount protected group routes, check active membership, create/edit expenses, and aggregate summaries. This router also mounts group-management routes. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `parseMoney(value, allowZero=false): number` | Validate decimal-text input and obtain integer cents. |
| Group Bill Splitting | `splitBill(totalCents, mode, input, memberIds): Share[]` | Calculate deterministic equal shares or validate exact custom amounts. |
| Bill Import | `DocumentExtractor.extract(file, defaultCurrency): Promise<Extraction>` | Return editable candidates via `OpenAiDocumentExtractor` or `extractStatement`. |
| Bill Import | `FxProvider.quote(from, to, date): Promise<ExchangeQuote>` | Return a validated historical quote through `FrankfurterFxProvider`. |
| Expense Management — Android | `LedgerRepository.previewCsv(text, statementCurrency?)` | Parse supported CSV rows on the device. |
| Expense Management — Android | `LedgerRepository.previewDocument(fileName, mimeType, bytes, localOnly=false)` | Validate a document and request backend extraction. `localOnly=true` selects backend statement parsing, not an offline Android path. |
| Expense Management — Android | `LedgerRepository.review(rows, existing)` → `LedgerDomain.review` | Validate rows and calculate local/within-import duplicate evidence. |
| Expense Management — Android | `LedgerRepository.commitImport(rows, source, fileName, requestId): Int` | Recheck decisions and quotes; atomically store selected records and request result in SQLite. |
| Expense Management — Android | `LedgerRepository.save(input, id?, revision?, requestId)`; `setBaseCurrency(currency)` | Save/edit local records or recalculate reporting amounts with local revision/transaction guarantees. |

#### Planned Interfaces — Group Bill Splitting

The following proposed contracts support UC-04/UC-05 and later repayment work. They are not implemented routes. Personal-bill reuse and extended split previews still require a separate contract that respects the installation-local source data; the current backend cannot fetch a personal record by account/source ID.

| Proposed interface | Input | Intended result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/split-sessions` | Reviewed itemized expense/session input | 201 `{session}` after owner, reconciliation, and membership checks. |
| `POST /api/split-sessions/{sessionId}/claims` | `unitId, action, version, operationKey` | 200 `{state, sequence}`; 409 for taken unit/stale version, 403 for releasing another member's unit. |
| `POST /api/split-sessions/{sessionId}/finalize` | `version, operationKey` | Finalized expense/allocation once all required units reconcile; retry-safe posting. |
| `GET /api/groups/{groupId}/snapshot` | Authorized group ID | Consistent `{expenses, claims, balances, sequence}` for recovery; balances require the future settlement model. |
| `GET /api/operations/{operationKey}` | Operation key and session | The authorized caller's operation result, or 404; never expose another caller's operation. |
| `POST /api/groups/{groupId}/repayments` | `toUserId, amount, operationKey` | A repayment awaiting recipient confirmation. |
| `POST /api/repayments/{repaymentId}/confirm` | Repayment ID and recipient session | Confirmed repayment and recalculated net balances. |
| Authenticated WebSocket subscription | Ledger session and group ID | A subscription only after identity and membership validation. |
| Server event **`onGroupUpdated`** | Committed state/event and sequence | Ordered application of committed changes; duplicates ignored and gaps recovered through UC-05. |

### 3.6. Dependency Diagram

The original dependency diagram is retained as Figure 2. Component labels follow the correspondence table in Section 3.1. The current call/data relationships are:

- Android Expense Management calls Bill Import for document suggestions and FX quotes, and uses SQLite for personal records, duplicate review, conversion, and commit.
- Android account/group screens call User Management, Group and Invitation Management, and Group Bill Splitting through the backend's REST APIs.
- User Management owns users/sessions; Group and Invitation Management owns groups/invitations; Group Bill Splitting owns expenses and reads group membership/currency and public profiles. All three use MongoDB.
- Bill Import calls OpenAI Document Recognition, the backend PDF parser, and Exchange-rate Service. It saves no personal financial records in MongoDB.
- Group Bill Splitting currently has no personal-record or FX dependency and emits no group events.

![][image2]

**Figure 2 — Retained dependency diagram; structural differences remain.** Expense Management is drawn in the backend but runs on Android. Group and Invitation Management is missing. The Bill Import-to-Expense Management duplicate/commit calls, Group Bill Splitting-to-Expense Management source/save calls, direct group FX dependency, separate OCR/AI providers, single backend Database, and WebSocket event arrow are not current implementation relationships. Sections 3.1–3.4 specify the current boundaries and interfaces.

### 3.7. Sequence Diagrams

The five original sequence images are retained as Figures 3–7, with their original UC numbers and titles. The formal text distinguishes current behavior from proposed behavior. `onGroupUpdated` is used consistently as the proposed notification name shown in the figures; no group event is currently implemented. `requireSession(token)` and other conceptual calls in the images are schematic, while Section 3.4 lists the actual TypeScript/Kotlin entry points and HTTP contracts.

#### UC-01 — Import and Review a Receipt — Implemented Flow; Earlier Figure Retained

Expense Management submits a confirmed document to Bill Import at `POST /api/ledger/imports/preview`. OpenAI Document Recognition returns transaction suggestions with HTTP 200; review and duplicate checking happen on Android. The current guest route requires no Ledger session, and the backend persists no draft.

![][image3]

**Figure 3 — Retained UC-01 sequence.** The image instead shows authenticated `/api/imports/receipts`, a persisted draft, backend duplicate review, draft updates, and revision conflicts. Those endpoints and backend draft writes do not exist. Its OCR Service label maps to OpenAI Document Recognition. Moving the draft/review responsibilities to Android requires a future figure edit; the current sequence is specified in Section 2.5.

#### UC-02 — Resolve Duplicate Candidates — Implemented Flow; Earlier Figure Retained

Expense Management loads SQLite records, reviews duplicate evidence using `LedgerDomain.review`, and revalidates selected rows in `LedgerRepository.commitImport`. Required quotes are obtained before one atomic SQLite record/request write. Matching completed request IDs return the stored count.

![][image4]

**Figure 4 — Retained UC-02 sequence.** Backend `/api/imports/{draftId}/duplicates` and `/api/imports/{draftId}/commit`, persisted backend drafts, and HTTP 409 draft conflicts are not implemented. The corresponding operations are local; validation/replay conflicts raise `LedgerException`. The original figure's server and database locations remain incorrect for the current workflow.

#### UC-03 — Reuse and Split a Personal Bill — Planned

The proposed sequence reads a source record and its revision from Android SQLite, requests explicit approval to share selected fields, and submits that snapshot for backend validation. Android rechecks the local revision before final confirmation; Group Bill Splitting validates the submitted snapshot and group state, then saves an independent expense with retry-safe allocations. Preview and snapshot-save messages are proposed contracts, not implemented CP1 endpoints.

![][image5]

**Figure 5 — UC-03 proposed client-snapshot sequence; not implemented for CP1.** SQLite represents installation-local Android storage; MongoDB represents backend group state. There is no backend lookup of a personal source record. Group FX and the preview/snapshot-save contracts remain planned. The summary uses REST; automatic live group delivery is a separate planned capability.

#### UC-04 — Claim or Unclaim Receipt Items Live — Planned

Group Bill Splitting will authorize claims, enforce exclusive unit ownership, and commit allocation state, an operation result, and an event together. Only committed results will be acknowledged and published as `onGroupUpdated(event, sequence)`.

![][image6]

**Figure 6 — Retained UC-04 proposed sequence.** The claim endpoint, item-unit/session model, atomic event/operation persistence, and authenticated group subscriptions have not been implemented. The current receipt extractor returns totals rather than claimable item units. The figure expresses the intended future interactions under the same component/event names used in the text.

#### UC-05 — Recover Live State After Reconnect — Planned

The Android front-end will buffer live events while installing an authorized snapshot and sequence watermark, apply contiguous later events, and resolve pending operation keys before enabling new claims.

![][image7]

**Figure 7 — Retained UC-05 proposed sequence.** Authenticated group subscriptions, snapshot/replay endpoints, operation lookup, and sequence recovery are future contracts. Current group screens update through REST refresh, and the retained M1 Socket.IO relay does not implement this recovery protocol. Figure 7 and the formal text describe the same planned behavior.

### 3.8. Design of Non-Functional Requirements

#### NFR-1 — Financial Integrity

For shared expenses, `parseMoney` validates decimal text and `splitBill` operates on integer cents. Equal splits sort participant IDs before distributing remainder cents; custom shares must be nonnegative and sum exactly to the total. The unique group/creator/request index prevents repeated creation. Changed edits use conditional revision updates; identical edits return the existing record.

For personal records, Android performs minor-unit arithmetic and decimal FX conversion. Local request fingerprints bind retries to their content. SQLite transactions combine imported records with their request result and protect multi-record changes. Quote retrieval/validation completes before the record transaction. Invalid selected rows or unacknowledged duplicate candidates prevent the import.

Planned live sessions additionally require conditional unit ownership, atomic state/event/operation persistence, sequence-aware delivery, and retry-safe finalization/repayments. These guarantees must be implemented and tested before UC-04/UC-05 can be described as working.

#### NFR-2 — Access Control and Privacy

User Management verifies session hashes and expiry for protected API routes. Group routes check active membership; only the owner may delete a group, and only an expense's creator or the owner may edit it. Nonmembers receive 404 for inaccessible groups. Invitation preview is distinct from acceptance; the public landing page reveals only invitation context, not shared expenses.

Expense Management persists financial records only in the installation's SQLite database. Recognition occurs after explicit submission; the backend validates file size/type and keeps the OpenAI key server-side. The backend does not persist uploaded documents. CSV can be parsed on-device, and supported text PDFs can be parsed on the backend without external AI.

The current guest ledger endpoints have rate/concurrency limits but no Ledger-session authentication. Shared deployment of paid recognition requires authentication/quota integration; rate limiting alone does not meet that requirement. Release configuration requires HTTPS. Future live subscriptions must add equivalent session/membership enforcement and WSS; the retained M1 socket is not evidence of that protection.

#### NFR-3 — Real-Time Responsiveness

Current Android work runs in background coroutines. The service bounds document size, import row count, simultaneous extraction, and upstream wait time; quote caches reduce repeated FX requests. Group summary aggregation returns all-expense totals with at most 50 recent expense cards. Current cross-device updates require an explicit REST refresh.

Planned live synchronization requires committed `onGroupUpdated` events, sequence-gap detection, snapshot recovery, and pending-operation lookup as specified in UC-04/UC-05. The 2-second update and 5-second recovery targets require measurement under the stated load; they are not current performance claims.
